round1_to_round2.mean_ladder_shift: P(close>=K) fell ~0.5-1.3 pts from K=202 to K=506 (P>=338 0.505 -> 0.492, P>=405 0.354 -> 0.342); tails and the 1-month ladder essentially unchanged (1m P>=337.5 0.500 -> 0.499).
round1_to_round2.what_drove_it: All five accepted the evidence-based corrections (convert $3.75B, pro forma net cash ~$1.3-1.5B / ~$1.9-2.0B by Sep-2027 instead of $1.8-3.0B, GAAP SBC 27%, Databricks >$7B/>80%, stale FOMC odds). Agents 2 and 4 cut their multiple from 14x to 13.5x; agents 1 and 5 stayed at 12.5x; agent_3 raised NTM revenue to $9.6B. Net: the high fair values (331, 340) came down, the low ones barely moved, so the group converged ~$5-6 lower.
round1_to_round2.overshoot_check: Part of the move rests on a round-1 supervisor error I now correct: the 'DDOG ~10.6x at 20% growth' peer point (from agent_5's source, repeated in my round-1 resolution) is wrong. Datadog trades ~22x LTM / ~18x NTM on ~24% NTM growth (Multiples.vc, EV $93B, LTM rev $4.2B; DDOG $272.68 on 2026-09-30). The peer band for a mid/high-20s grower is therefore ~8x (MDB) to ~18x (DDOG), centre ~13-13.5x, which removes one argument for 12.5x. I keep 13x and put back a little of the mid-ladder decline.
round1_to_round2.convergence: Mid-ladder spread across agents narrowed (P>=338 range 0.023 in round 2 vs 0.020 in round 1; fair-value range halved from $30 to $15); upper-tail disagreement remains (agent_5 P>=675 0.029 vs agents 2 and 4 ~0.085).

Kept 12.5x (Databricks argument), a reasoned disagreement; FV $316 -> $317. Ladder moved only ~0.5 pt at the top: consistent with its FV change.

Raised NTM revenue to $9.6B, fixed net cash, SBC and the two-case litigation. Traced the discounted Databricks SQL claim to the company's Aug 13 release (Lakehouse warehousing >$1.5B run-rate, >100%; verified). Its upper tail (P>=675 0.029, P>=844 0.006) is far thinner than the others' and than a 62%-vol stock that went $118 -> $384 in five months implies. '10-year near 5%' is unsourced.

disagreements.resolution: Agent_2 is right on the fact: Datadog is ~$96B market cap / $93B EV on $4.2B LTM revenue = 22x LTM and ~18x NTM at ~24% NTM growth; the 10.6x figure (also in my round-1 resolution) is wrong. MongoDB at ~8x NTM on ~19% bounds the low end. For a mid/high-20s grower with 126% NRR and ~25% FCF margin the band centre is ~13-13.5x; 12.5x is defensible only as a regime/Databricks haircut, not from the peer line. Each 0.5x is ~$12/share.

Not settleable by search. The stock's 62% realized vol and $118 -> $384 move argue against agent_5's thin tail, but the new converts and capped calls do not cap the stock. I keep the mean on the tail strikes.

one_month_reasoning: No SNOW earnings before 2026-10-30 (Q3 FY27 undated, early December likely); the convert closes Oct 1 with hedging already in the price, the Oct 13 MTD is a filing and the older action's ruling is small, and hyperscaler prints and the Oct 28 FOMC (hike odds ~36% post-PCE) are two-sided, so I keep the forecasters' near-symmetric round-2 mean.
confidence_reason: I settled one disagreement that matters (the DDOG 10.6x peer point behind 12.5x is wrong; DDOG is ~18x NTM), but the peer band (8-18x) is wide and the correction is worth only ~$3-5 on the group fair value, so I nudge the middle strikes up ~0.2-0.8 pt and do not claim the mean should be replaced.
thesis_break_reason: All five sit at $210-220. At ~$215 (-36%, ~9x NTM sales) the market would be pricing product growth back toward 20-25%, NRR toward 115-120%, or clear share loss to Databricks, whose warehousing line is $1.5B growing >100%. Confirm with a guide-down at the December or Feb/Mar print; a macro liquidation reached $118 in April 2026 without a fundamental break.
key_drivers: Reacceleration durability: Q2 FY27 product revenue +37%, Q3 guide +37-38%, FY27 $6.07B (+36%), RPO $9.0B +30%, NRR 126%; the FY28 guide in Feb/Mar 2027 (consensus ~+28%) is the test.
Multiple: ~16-17x NTM sales today, expected to settle ~13x on ~$9.6B Sep-2027 NTM revenue; peer band 8x (MDB) to 18x (DDOG), so each 0.5x is ~$12/share.
Competition: Databricks >$7B run-rate, >80% growth, Lakehouse warehousing $1.5B growing >100% (company PR, Aug 13, 2026).
Margins and dilution: product GM guide cut to 74% on AI mix while op margin guide rose to 14.5%; GAAP SBC ~27% of revenue.
Capital structure: $3.75B 0% converts (conversion $484/$500, capped calls to $820.30) leave pro forma net cash only ~$1.3-1.5B, ~$2.0B by Sep-2027.

fair_value.reason: 13x EV/NTM sales on ~$9.6B Sep-2027 NTM revenue = $124.8B + ~$2.0B net cash = ~$127B / 388M diluted shares = ~$327; SBC-aware FCF (~45-50x ~$2.4B) ~$300-315 and NTM P/E (~80x ~$4.0) ~$315-320 pull the blend to ~$322. summary: Round 2 converged: all five accepted the round-1 corrections, fair values narrowed to $313-328 (mean $317.8, from $323.4) and the ladders moved down ~1 pt in the middle. One of those corrections overshot: the 'Datadog ~10.6x' peer anchor behind the 12.5x multiples is wrong (Datadog is ~22x LTM / ~18x NTM on ~24% growth), so a ~13x centre and ~$322 fair value fit better, and I nudge the middle strikes up ~0.5 pt. Median stays about at spot ($337.50): ~28% revenue growth is offset by compression from ~16-17x toward ~13x NTM sales, with Databricks' warehousing line ($1.5B growing >100%) and the AI-driven gross-margin cut (75% to 74%) as the main risks. Low-confidence update; thesis break ~$215; no earnings before early December.
